title: Boss: The Owner's Report
story: The owner's final request combines everything: customers, spend, and their rank within city.
goal: For each customer with at least one delivered order and a city: show name, city, spent and city_rank (1 = biggest spender in that city, RANK), ordered by city, then city_rank, then name.

tests.label: Hidden check on other data

hints: CTE for spend, then join to customers and add RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY city ...).
Filter out NULL cities in WHERE. The final ORDER BY has three keys.

WITH spend AS (SELECT o.customer_id, SUM(o.qty * p.price) AS spent FROM orders o JOIN products p ON p.id = o.product_id WHERE o.status = 'delivered' GROUP BY o.customer_id) SELECT c.name, c.city, s.spent, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY c.city ORDER BY s.spent DESC) AS city_rank FROM spend s JOIN customers c ON c.id = s.customer_id WHERE c.city IS NOT NULL ORDER BY c.city, city_rank, c.name;
socratic: What does PARTITION BY c.city do?
Why is the NULL city skipped?
explain: In one sentence: what does this query do, and why does it need the a CTE?
solution: WITH spend AS (SELECT o.customer_id, SUM(o.qty * p.price) AS spent FROM orders o JOIN products p ON p.id = o.product_id WHERE o.status = 'delivered' GROUP BY o.customer_id) SELECT c.name, c.city, s.spent, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY c.city ORDER BY s.spent DESC) AS city_rank FROM spend s JOIN customers c ON c.id = s.customer_id WHERE c.city IS NOT NULL ORDER BY c.city, city_rank, c.name;
alt: WITH spend AS (SELECT o.customer_id, SUM(o.qty * p.price) AS spent FROM orders o JOIN products p ON p.id = o.product_id WHERE o.status = 'delivered' GROUP BY o.customer_id), j AS (SELECT c.name, c.city, s.spent FROM spend s JOIN customers c ON c.id = s.customer_id WHERE c.city IS NOT NULL) SELECT name, city, spent, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY city ORDER BY spent DESC) AS city_rank FROM j ORDER BY city, city_rank, name;
